title: Runner-Up Digit in a Mixed String
statement:
You get a string s made of lowercase letters and digits. Look only at the digits.

Return the second largest distinct digit that appears in s, as a number. If there are fewer than two different digits, return -1.

examples.why: The distinct digits are 9, 5 and 3. The repeated 9 does not count as a second 9.
Digits 1 and 0. Zero is a real digit, so it is the runner-up.

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters and digits
hints: Only ten different digits exist. You could just record which ones appear.
Or keep the best and second-best distinct digits seen so far in one pass.
When a new digit beats the best, the old best becomes second. When it equals the best, ignore it. When it falls strictly between, it becomes second.

explain.intuition:
This is the classic "top two" scan with one twist: distinct. Keep first and second, both starting at -1. A digit bigger than first pushes the old first down to second. A digit strictly between them replaces second. A digit equal to first must be ignored, or a repeated 9 would become its own runner-up.

Since there are only ten possible digits, marking which appear in a boolean array and reading it from 9 down is just as good and even harder to get wrong.
steps: For each character that is a digit d:
If d > first, set second = first and first = d.
Else if first > d > second, set second = d.
pitfalls: Accepting d == first as a new second, so "aa77a" returns 7.
Using 0 as the "nothing yet" value. Then "r1t0" cannot tell a real 0 from no digit.
Forgetting to shift the old best down to second when a bigger digit arrives.

solutions.title: Mark the digits that appear
solutions.idea: Record which of the ten digits occur, then walk from 9 down and return the second one found.

solutions.title: Track the top two in one pass
solutions.idea: Keep the best and second-best distinct digits; ignore a digit equal to the current best.

followups: Return the k-th largest distinct digit. Which of the two solutions generalises more easily?
Find the second largest distinct number formed by maximal runs of digits, like 42 in "a42b7".
